subject: science
title: Animals, Including Humans
description: Why humans and some animals need nutrition from what they eat, the different food groups, and how skeletons and muscles support, protect and move the body.

objectives.statement: Identify that animals, including humans, need the right types and amount of nutrition, and that they cannot make their own food; they get nutrition from what they eat.
Identify that humans and some other animals have skeletons and muscles for support, protection and movement.

items.prompt: Where do animals, including humans, get their nutrition from?

items.statement: Unlike plants, animals cannot make their own food.

items.prompt: Why do humans need to eat a variety of different foods?
options: to get the different nutrients the body needs

items.statement: A green plant can make its own food using sunlight, but a dog cannot.

items.prompt: Which of these is a source of food nutrition?
Which food group gives us most of our energy and includes bread, rice and pasta?
Which of these foods is a good source of protein for building the body?
Which food group are fruits and vegetables an important source of vitamins from?

items.statement: Eating a balanced diet means eating the right types and amounts of different foods.
A meal made only of sweets and cake gives your body all the nutrients it needs.

items.prompt: Name a food group that helps keep bones and teeth strong, found in milk and cheese.
Name one job that the skeleton does for the body.
items.answer: Any of: support, protection, or helping the body move

items.prompt: Which part of the skeleton protects the brain?
Which bones protect the heart and lungs?

items.statement: An animal with a skeleton of bones inside its body has a bony skeleton.
Every animal in the world has a skeleton of bones inside its body.

items.prompt: What is joined to bones and pulls on them to make the body move?

items.statement: Muscles work by pulling on bones, not by pushing them.

items.prompt: To bend and straighten your arm, muscles work in pairs. When one muscle contracts (shortens), the other one...
What do we call the place where two bones meet and the body can bend?
